Both tracts encompass plateaus of Tongue River strata, with abrupt slopes along the main drainages and along the coulees which penetrate into the highlands. Tract II is an outlier of the Tongue River member between Tullock Creek and Sarpy Creek. The outlier was isolated from the main part of the member by the creeks as they cut downward through the layers of the Tongue River member into the Lebo shale member (Figure II-2). Tract III contains that part of the Tongue River member contiguous to the north boundary of the Crow Indian Reservation and lying between Sarpy Creek and East Fork of Sarpy Creek, with the eastern limit being the boundary of the Crow Ceded Area.
The rocks of the Tongue River member are tan, yellow, and gray interlayered sandstone, siltstone, claystone, and mudstone. They were formed from the stream-laid sediments of the ancient floodplains. Two stray coal seams (each 3 to 5 feet thick) and the two lowermost thick seams of coal in the Tongue River member, the Robinson (about 20 feet thick) and the Rosebud-McKay (about 30 feet thick), have been preserved in this area. The Rosebud-McKay is 50 to 120 feet above the Robinson seam. The Robinson seam occurs over most of Tracts II and III. The Rosebud-McKay seam has been burned over most of Tract III and about a third of Tract III. In the eastern part of Tract III, the Rosebud and McKay seams are separated by a parting of one to five feet, with a few drill holes showing a parting of 30 to 40 feet.
